lesson.title: Vaccinations
lesson.title_ar: القسم العلمي (6): التطعيم واللقاحات (جينر وباستور والأبحاث الحديثة)

lines: Introduction: Before the late 18th century, thousands of people died every year from such diseases as smallpox, typhoid and cholera. Doctors tried unsuccessfully to treat patients with these diseases while scientists struggled to find suitable cures. The big breakthrough came from an unexpected source: an unknown country doctor in England.

Box 1 (left — Dr Edward Jenner): Dr Edward Jenner was experimenting with ways of vaccinating against smallpox when he noticed that people working with cows did not suffer the disease. On May 14th, 1796, Jenner successfully used the first vaccine against smallpox to immunize a patient. The word vaccine comes from the Latin cow, because Jenner's vaccine was developed from cowpox, a disease similar to smallpox but only found in cattle. Jenner's work with a cowpox vaccine was the first scientific attempt to control a disease by immunization.

Box 1 (right — Dr Louis Pasteur): A century later, the next significant development was made by a French chemist, Dr Louis Pasteur. He developed Jenner's work and showed that diseases are spread by germs. He also proved that vaccination using a very weak form of the disease could lead to immunity. Pasteur's breakthrough came in 1885 when he treated a boy who had been bitten by a rabid dog. Although Pasteur was successful, many other doctors were against the idea of vaccination. They felt that it was dangerous. They were soon proved wrong, and by the 20th century vaccines were commonplace.

Box 2 (AIDS research): AIDS is one of the most feared diseases in history. Millions of dollars are being spent on research into developing a vaccine against AIDS. Scientists think that AIDS developed from the blood of monkeys in Central Africa. The first cases of AIDS in humans were diagnosed in the early 1970s. Once AIDS had infected people, transmission around the world was rapid. Modern drugs have helped with some aspects of the illness, but they do not provide a cure. The only long-term hope is in the development of a vaccine.
We need the modern-day equivalents of scientists like Jenner and Pasteur.
Discussion: Is it right to introduce a disease - even a weak form - into a person's body?

simple_explain.html:
• الاسمان المشتقان في جدول 6 D: للفعلين الأولين اسمان في النص:
    • immunize ← immunity (المناعة المكتسبة) وimmunization (عملية التمنيع/التلقيح).
    • vaccinate ← vaccine (اللقاح نفسه) وvaccination (التطعيم باللقاح).
  • مناقشة أخلاقية (PB ص 70): إدخال صورة ضعيفة أو آمنة من الميكروب يُدرّب جهاز المناعة لتكوين وقاية طويلة الأمد، وهو صحيح طبياً متى ثبت أمان اللقاح مخبرياً وسريرياً وبموافقة المريض/أسرته.

example.html: Etymology fact: The word vaccine derives from Latin vacca (= cow), because Jenner used mild cowpox to protect humans from deadly smallpox.

activities.prompt_literal: SCIENCE 6 A Read the texts and choose the best heading for each.
activities.prompt_ar: اختر الحرف الدال على أنسب عنوان (a أو b أو c) لكل قسم من الأقسام الأربعة (WB ص 102):

items.prompt: Introduction [a Vaccination in history / b The need for vaccines / c Diseases that kill]: ______
Box 1 (left) [a A vaccine for smallpox / b The life of Jenner / c Smallpox and cowpox]: ______
Box 1 (right) [a The cause of disease / b Giving disease to prevent disease / c The life of Pasteur]: ______
Box 2 [a The rise of AIDS / b Modern drugs and AIDS / c The search for an AIDS vaccine]: ______

hints: Introduction: b (الحاجة الماسة للقاحات) · Box 1 left: a · Box 1 right: b (التحصين بنسخة ضعيفة من المرض) · Box 2: c.

activities.prompt_literal: B Number these stages in the history of vaccination in order. (1–9)
activities.prompt_ar: رقّم المراحل التسع في تاريخ التطعيم من 1 إلى 9 حسب الترتيب الزمني (WB ص 102):

items.prompt: ______ Jenner noticed that people working with cows did not suffer from smallpox.
______ AIDS developed from the blood of Central African monkeys.
______ Modern drugs help to control AIDS.
______ Pasteur showed that diseases were spread by germs.
______ Pasteur successfully treated a boy who had been bitten by a rabid dog.

hints: قبل القرن 18 (1) ← ملاحظة جينر وتطعيمه 1796 (2–3) ← أبحاث باستور وعلاجه 1885 (4–5) ← نشأة الإيدز في القرود ثم تشخيصه بالسبعينيات وانتشاره ثم الأدوية الحديثة (6–9).

activities.prompt_literal: C These words from the texts are related in meaning. Explain the differences. (1 doctors / scientists printed; solve 2–8)
activities.prompt_ar: وضّح الفرق الدلالي بين كل زوجين من المصطلحات الطبية 2–8 (WB ص 102–103):

items.question: 2 treat vs cure
items.model_answer: Treat means give medical care/medicine to try to help an ill patient (not always successfully); cure means heal completely and remove the disease.
items.explain_ar: العلاج محاولة تخفيف المرض أو مداواته، أما الشفاء فهو القضاء التام على العلة.

items.question: 3 cowpox vs smallpox
items.model_answer: Smallpox is a deadly human disease; cowpox is a similar mild disease found only in cattle (cows), used by Jenner to make a smallpox vaccine.
items.explain_ar: جدري البشر القاتل مقابل جدري البقر الخفيف.

items.question: 4 disease vs germ
items.model_answer: A germ is the tiny living cause/organism that spreads illness; a disease is the illness itself suffered by the body.
items.explain_ar: الجرثومة سبب والمرض هو الأثر والحالة.

items.question: 5 infection vs transmission
items.model_answer: Infection happens when germs enter a body and make it sick; transmission is the spreading/passing of a disease from person to person across places.
items.explain_ar: العدوى إصابة الفرد، والانتقال انتشارها بين الناس.

items.question: 6 vaccine vs disease
items.model_answer: A disease harms or kills a patient; a vaccine is a mild/weak preventive substance given beforehand to build immunity against that disease.

items.question: 7 diagnose vs treat
items.model_answer: Diagnose means identify what illness a patient has; treat means give medical care/medicine afterwards for that illness.
items.explain_ar: التشخيص هو تحديد الداء ثم يتلوه العلاج.

items.question: 8 breakthrough vs development
items.model_answer: A breakthrough is a sudden major discovery solving a difficult barrier; a development is a step-by-step improvement or progress building on existing work.
items.explain_ar: الاكتشاف الفارق المفاجئ مقابل التطوير التدريجي المتراكم.

hints: اعتمد على السياق الطبي لكل كلمة في فقرتها داخل PB ص 70.

questions.stem: Where does the word 'vaccine' come from, and why (PB page 70)?

options.text: From the Latin word for cow, because Jenner developed the first vaccine from cowpox.
From the Greek word for vacuum, because germs live in outer space.
options.why_wrong: vacuum كلمة من درس الضوء والصوت بمعنى الفراغ ولا صلة لها بالتطعيم.

options.text: From Arabic meaning 'ashes of a plant'.
options.why_wrong: معنى أشنان/رماد النبات يخص كلمة alkali في الدرس الأول.
جينر هو من استعمل لقاح جدري البقر عام 1796، وعمل باستور كان بعده بقرن (1885).

hints: انظر المربع الأوسط الأيسر: The word vaccine comes from the Latin...
questions.explain: أُخذت الكلمة vaccine من الكلمة اللاتينية التي تعني البقرة لأن جينر صنع لقاح الجدري من مرض جدري البقر الخفيف.

questions.stem: According to WB Science 6 D, which noun-verb set matches 'transmission' and 'diagnosis' correctly?

options.why_wrong: هاتان صيغتان خطأ غير موجودتين في الإنجليزية.
treatable صفة وليست الاسم المطلوب في الجدول (treatment).
experimental صفة وليست اسم/فعل جدول 6 D.

hints: راجع الأفعال التي تأخذ -ssion و-sis في الجدول 6 D.
questions.explain: الفعل transmit اسمه transmission، والفعل diagnose اسمه diagnosis.
